floor_history.headline: Recon: baseline floor 8, gap is prologue callee-save ORDER (not RA); killed H-s1 count-first reorder (8→13); frontier H-s2/s3/s4 on axes that shift first-write sequence without cheat-siblings' pin+dum

frontier.hypothesis: H-s2: hoist `saved = g_cd_callback_a;` to the first assignment (before any arg reference) will change the earliest sw insertion and shift a1/a2's callee-save copies ahead of a0's.
frontier.mechanism: sched1's arg-copy scheduling picks first-use ordering off the RTL insertion sequence; if s5's first-use comes before any arg reference, GCC may bind the arg-move ordering to non-a0 first.
frontier.next_probe: Reorder to `saved = g_cd_callback_a; idx = a0 & 0xFF; base = g_cd_sector_buf; elem = base + idx; count = 3;` and sandbox; measure sw-order delta.

frontier.hypothesis: H-s3: replacing `base = g_cd_sector_buf; elem = base + idx;` with `elem = &g_cd_sector_buf[a0 & 0xFF];` (drop base + inline idx) reduces pseudo count and matches the sibling's shape, potentially reordering the andi/sll interleave in the prologue.
frontier.mechanism: Fewer named locals => different first-use graph; sibling's shape (minus the pin+dummy cheat) may naturally schedule the andi where target has it (post move-s4, pre count-init).
frontier.next_probe: Rewrite as `elem = &g_cd_sector_buf[a0 & 0xFF];` keep `idx` only if needed for later `idx != 1` compare (or fold to `(a0 & 0xFF) != 1`); sandbox.

frontier.hypothesis: H-s4: rewrite loop as `do { ... } while (--count != -1);` (removing the label + goto) may steer sched1's basic-block boundaries so save-slot insertions land in target order.
frontier.mechanism: Basic-block structure determines where GCC inserts prologue insns relative to loop entry; a natural-loop form may relocate the boundary that currently forces sw s0 to the tail.
frontier.next_probe: Rewrite loop control to `do { ... } while (--count != -1);` preserving all inner semantics; sandbox and inspect sw sequence.
